h: Lochside Extras Worth Making Time For
p: Loch Lomond Shores is a ready-made day out in its own right, with shops, places to eat and the loch lapping right up to the promenade, so the aquarium slots in nicely as one part of a bigger plan. Allow a couple of hours inside, a bit longer if you catch a keeper talk or a feeding session, and save the rest of the day for the great outdoors.

Boat trips are the classic add-on. Cruises leave from Balloch through the season, and seeing the islands and mountains from the water is a cracking way to show kids the scale of the place. If you'd rather keep your feet on land, Balloch Castle Country Park is just across the River Leven, with lawns, woodland paths and views up the loch.

Fancy a short climb? Duncryne Hill near Gartocharn, nicknamed the Dumpling, is a small hill with a huge view and suits families with younger walkers. Further up the east shore, Conic Hill above Balmaha is a bigger outing, but the panorama over the loch and its islands is one of the finest in this part of Scotland.

The weather here changes fast, so pack waterproofs and a warm layer even in summer, and midge repellent if you're heading out on a still evening. A dry, warm aquarium is a brilliant thing to have up your sleeve when the rain sweeps in off the hills.

Balloch also sits at the southern gateway to Loch Lomond and The Trossachs National Park, so if you're carrying on north, the drive up the west shore towards Luss and Tarbet is beautiful and well worth taking slowly.
